tells.1: none. The concrete details (180 covers, six cooks, Luis, the four-year sous chef, 100% health coverage) read as real. At most, 'without turning the kitchen into a pressure cooker' is a bit of a stock phrase.
tells.2: Template formatting with bolded 'What you'll do / What we're after' labels, plus the triplet 'real days off, nights that actually end, and a schedule you can plan a life around' and the repeated 'real' ('real say').
tells.3: Formatting is cleaner, but it keeps the vague reassurance 'That means real days off and nights that actually end, so you can plan a life around the schedule' instead of giving a concrete fact.

reason: Version 1 replaces generic lifestyle promises with specifics a candidate can actually weigh: covers, crew size, a four-day week, promotion stories, and benefits. That makes it the most credible and human. Versions 2 and 3 share the same boilerplate, and 2's bold-header template feels the most generated.
